QUSHAYRI:v3p347/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p347/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p347/r1.claim: The basmalah needs a noble hearing untouched by backbiting and a noble heart undisturbed by heedlessness or absence.
QUSHAYRI:v3p347/r1.anchor: كلمة عزيزة تحتاج في سماعها إلى سمع عزيز لم يستعمل في سماع الغيبة

QUSHAYRI:v3p347/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p347/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p347/r2.claim: The Inevitable Reality names the Resurrection because it brings each person face to face with the good and evil of their deeds.
QUSHAYRI:v3p347/r2.anchor: اسم للقيامة لأنها تحق كل إنسان بعمله خيره وشره

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3369#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3369#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3369#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says al-Haqqa is one of the names for the Day of Resurrection.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3369#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : الحاقة قال : من اسماء يوم القيامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p114/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p114/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p114/r4.claim: Alternatively, if the clauses connect, Thamūd and ʿĀd denied the Resurrection; “the Striker” is a synonym for the Reality, brought forward instead of a pronoun to explain its terrifying force.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p114/r4.anchor: فعدل إلى إظهار اسم ( القارعة ) لأن ( القارعة ) مرادفة

NAHHAS:v5p19/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p19/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p19/r1.claim: الحاقة is nominative as the opening subject.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r1.claim: الحاقة is an active participle from حقّ, meaning a real existent; Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatada identify it as Resurrection and requital.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r1.anchor: الحاقة اسم فاعل، من حق الشيء يحق إذا كان صحيح الوجود،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r2.claim: Some take الحاقة as a verbal noun like العاقبة and العافية, meaning the possessor of truth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r2.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين: الحاقة مصدر كالعاقبة والعافية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r3.claim: They say Resurrection is named الحاقة because it reveals the realities of things.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وغيره: سميت القيامة حاقة، لأنها تبدي حقائق الأشياء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p345/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p345/r1.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p345/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the Resurrection is called the Inevitable because the decisive realities of things become evident in it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p345/r1.anchor: قال الفراء إنما قيل لها حاقة لأن فيها حواق الأمور

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p345/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p345/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p345/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj says it is called the Inevitable because it makes every person receive the result of their good and evil deeds.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p345/r2.anchor: وقال الزجاج إنما سميت الحاقة لأنها تحق كل إنسان بعمله من خير وشر

JISHUMI:v10p7051/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r1.claim: A report promises an easy reckoning from God for anyone who recites Sūrat al-Ḥāqqah.
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r1.anchor: من قرأ سورة (الحاقة) حاسبه الله حسابا يسيرا

JISHUMI:v10p7051/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r2.claim: After the Resurrection warning in al-Qalam and the command to endure the unbelievers' abuse, al-Ḥāqqah opens with the Resurrection and its events.
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r2.anchor: ولما ذكر في سورة (القلم) حديث القيامة ووعيد الكفار،

JISHUMI:v10p7051/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r6.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r6.claim: One explanation calls al-Ḥāqqah a name for the Resurrection.
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r6.anchor: إنه اسم من أسماء القيامة، عن الأصم

JISHUMI:v10p7051/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r7.claim: Another derives it from “truth”: God's promise and threat become true at the Resurrection.
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r7.anchor: لأن وعده ووعيده يحق فيها، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v10p7051/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says it is so called because the realities of deeds become clear there.
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r8.anchor: لأنه يتبين فيها حقائق الأعمال فسميت الحاقة

JISHUMI:v10p7051/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r9.speaker: ابن الأنباري
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r9.claim: It can mean the inevitable event, when each person necessarily receives recompense for his deeds.
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r9.anchor: الحاقة: الواجبة، من قولهم: حق، أي: وجب

JISHUMI:v10p7051/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r10.speaker: الكسائي
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r10.claim: Al-Kisāʾī calls it the Day of truth; other explanations say it is a true event with no denial or a day that overpowers the unbelievers.
JISHUMI:v10p7051/r10.anchor: وقيل: سميت الحاقة؛ لأنها يوم الحق، عن الكسائي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r1.claim: Al-Haqqah is the Hour whose coming is certain and unavoidable, with no doubt.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r1.anchor: الساعة الواجبة الوقوع الثابتة المجيء ، التي هي آتية لا ريب فيها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r2.claim: Another explanation is that it is the Hour in which the realities of reckoning, reward, and punishment are realized.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r2.anchor: أو التي فيها حواق الأمور من الحساب والثواب والعقاب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r3.claim: A further explanation is that matters become known in their true reality then; haqq means to know something's truth.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r3.anchor: أو التي تحق فيها الأمور ، أي : تعرف على الحقيقة ، من قولك لا أحق هذا ، أي : لا أعرف حقيقته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r4.claim: The verb of becoming real is attributed to the Hour, although in fact the people who experience it are the ones to whom it applies.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r5.claim: Al-Haqqah is the subject and ma al-haqqah its predicate; the underlying wording is al-Haqqah ma hiya, with the explicit noun replacing the pronoun for emphasis and awe.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r5.anchor: وارتفاعها على الابتداء وخبرها { ما الحآقة } والأصل : الحاقة ما هي ، أي أي شيء هي تفخيما لشأنها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r6.claim: Ma adraka asks what could make one know the Hour's nature; its greatness exceeds anyone's knowledge or imagination, however one imagines it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r6.anchor: وكيفما قدرت حالها فهي أعظم من ذلك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r7.claim: Ma is nominative, while adraka is suspended from taking an object because it contains an interrogative.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r7.anchor: و ( ما ) في موضع الرفع على الابتداء . و { أدراك } معلق عنه لتضمنه معنى الاستفهام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r8.claim: Al-Qari'ah means the striking calamity: it terrifies people, splits the sky, crushes and scatters mountains and earth, and extinguishes stars.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r8.anchor: القارعة ) التي تقرع الناس بالأفزاع والأهوال ، والسماء بالانشقاق والإنفطار ، والأرض والجبال بالدك والنسف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r9.claim: Calling it al-Qari'ah in place of a pronoun evokes the blow itself and further intensifies the description of the Hour's severity.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r9.anchor: وضعت موضع الضمير لتدل على معنى القرع . في الحاقة : زيادة في وصف شدتها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r10.claim: After magnifying the Hour, the discourse recounts those who denied it and what befell them, warning the Meccans about the outcome of denial.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r10.anchor: ولما ذكرها وفخمها أتبع ذكر من كذب بها وما حل بهم بسبب التكذيب ، تذكيرا لأهل مكة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r1.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r1.claim: He explains الحاقة as the arrival of what was truly promised or threatened.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r1.anchor: ما حق من الوعد والوعيد بحلوله , وهو معنى قول ابن بحر

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r2.speaker: الجمهور
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r2.claim: Most commentators identify الحاقة as the Resurrection, when promise and threat are realized.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r2.anchor: القيامة التي يستحق فيها الوعد والوعيد , قاله الجمهور

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r3.speaker: قتادة ويحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r3.claim: They explain its name by the realization of reward and punishment for obedience and sins.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r3.anchor: استحقاق الوعد والوعيد بالجزاء على الطاعات والمعاصي , وهو معنى قول قتادة ويحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r4.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r4.claim: He says the name reflects the disclosure of realities.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r4.anchor: لأن فيها حقائق الأمور , قاله الكلبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r5.claim: A further explanation is that believers rightly fear the event.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r5.anchor: لأن حقا على المؤمن أن يخافها

MUJAHID:v2p691/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p691/r1.speaker: عكرمة
MUJAHID:v2p691/r1.claim: He identifies الحاقة as the Resurrection.
MUJAHID:v2p691/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله عز وجل ﴿ الحاقة ﴾ القيامة

MUQATIL:69:1-4/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:69:1-4/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:69:1-4/r1.claim: Al-Ḥāqqah is the Hour in which the realities of deeds are established: believers' deeds and disbelievers' deeds alike become manifest and true.
MUQATIL:69:1-4/r1.anchor: يعني الساعة التي فيها حقائق الأعمال، يقول يحق للمؤمنين عملهم، ويحق للكافرين عملهم

MUQATIL:69:1-4/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:69:1-4/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:69:1-4/r3.claim: He identifies the Hour as al-Qāriʿah, the event denied by Thamūd and ʿĀd, and notes its parallel in Sūrat al-Qāriʿah.
MUQATIL:69:1-4/r3.anchor: ثم قال: هي القارعة، والساعة التي { كذبت } بها { ثمود وعاد بالقارعة }

NASAFI-FULL:v4p273#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p273#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p273#4/r1.claim: Al-Ḥāqqa is the Hour whose arrival is certain and unavoidable; the word derives from haqq, to be established or obligatory.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p273#4/r1.anchor: الساعة الواجبة الوقوع الثابتة المجئ التي هي آتيه لا ريب فيها من حق بحق بالكسر أي وجب

QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r1.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r1.claim: Al-Tabari says the Resurrection is called al-Haqqah because realities become manifest there.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r1.anchor: يريد القيامة سميت بذلك لأن الأمور تحق فيها قاله الطبري.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r2.claim: Other explanations say it is certain, assigns some people Paradise and others Hell, or makes each person deserve their deeds' recompense.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r2.anchor: وقيل: سميت حاقة لأنها تكون من غير شك. وقيل: سميت بذلك لأنها أحقت لأقوام الجنة

QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r3.speaker: الأزهري
QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r3.claim: Al-Azhari relates the name to prevailing in a dispute; Resurrection overcomes every opponent of God's true religion.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r3.anchor: وقال الأزهري: يقال حاققته فحققته أحقه أي غالبته فغلبته.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r4.claim: Al-Haqqah, al-Haqqah with tāʾ, and al-Haqq are three forms with the same meaning; al-Kisaʾi and al-Muʾarrij call it the Day of Truth.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r4.anchor: والحاقة والحقة والحق ثلاث لغات بمعنى. وقال الكسائي والمؤرج: الحاقة يوم الحق.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r5.claim: The Arabs say someone fled when he realized the other person was right.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:1-3/r5.anchor: وتقول العرب: لما عرف الحقة مني هرب.

SAMIN-DURR:69:1/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:69:1/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:69:1/r1.claim: الحاقة is the first subject; ما is a second subject and الحاقة its predicate, with the whole clause serving as the first predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:69:1/r1.anchor: مبتدأ و " ما " مبتدأ ثان، و " الحاقة " خبره، والجملة خبر الأول

SAMIN-DURR:69:1/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:69:1/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:69:1/r2.claim: الحاقة may be an active participle because it reveals realities; alternatively the event becomes real, it is fixed, or it overcomes disputants in religion.
SAMIN-DURR:69:1/r2.anchor: والحاقة فيها وجهان، أحدهما: أنه وصف اسم فاعل بمعنى: أنها تبدي حقائق الأشياء

SAMIN-DURR:69:1/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:69:1/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:69:1/r3.claim: A second morphological analysis takes الحاقة as a verbal noun like العاقبة and العافية.

RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r1.claim: All agree al-Ḥāqqah names the Resurrection; its root conveys something established and certain to arrive.
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r1.anchor: أجمعوا على أن الحاقة هي القيامة

RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r2.claim: One explanation says it is the event in which realities become known; the action is attributed to the Hour though people learn the truth.
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r2.anchor: أنها التي تحق فيها الأمور أي تعرف على الحقيقة

RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r3.claim: Another derives it from matters of verified truth: reward, punishment, and the other events of resurrection are all certain realities.
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r3.anchor: أنها ذوات الحواق من الأمور وهي الصادقة الواجبة الصدق

RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r4.claim: A fourth explanation equates al-Ḥāqqah with al-ḥaqqah, a more specific and compelling right, close in meaning to the first explanation.
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r4.anchor: بمعنى الحقة والحقة أخص من الحق وأوجب

RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r5.speaker: الليث
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r5.claim: Al-Layth glosses it as an event that descends and inevitably comes true, like the description of the Event as having no lie in its occurrence.
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r5.anchor: قال الليث : { الحاقة } النازلة التي حقت بالجارية

RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r6.claim: Another view calls it the Hour in which recompense becomes due for every error and guidance.
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r6.anchor: الساعة التي يحق فيها الجزاء على كل ضلال وهدى وهي القيامة

RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r7.claim: Another view calls it the time when the event is due to befall a people.
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r7.anchor: الوقت الذي يحق على القوم أن يقع بهم

RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r8.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj says it is the truth in which the outcomes of people's acts—reward and punishment—are realized rather than still awaited.
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r8.anchor: جميع آثار أعمال المكلفين فإن في ذلك اليوم يحصل الثواب والعقاب ويخرج عن حد الانتظار وهو قول الزجاج

RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r9.speaker: الأزهري
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r9.claim: Al-Azharī says it is named because it overcomes and defeats every opponent of God's religion, from the verb for prevailing in disputation.
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r9.anchor: قال الأزهري : والذي عندي في { الحاقة } أنها سميت بذلك

RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r10.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r10.claim: Abū Muslim derives al-Ḥāqqah as the active form of “the word of your Lord came due.”
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r10.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : { الحاقة } الفاعلة من حقت كلمة ربك

RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r11.claim: Syntactically, al-Ḥāqqah is the subject and “what is al-Ḥāqqah?” its predicate; repeating the noun instead of a pronoun magnifies the event.
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r11.anchor: فوضع الظاهر موضع المضمر لأنه أهول لها

RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r12.claim: “What could make you know?” means its true nature and terror exceed anyone's knowledge or imagination; however one pictures it, it is greater.
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r12.anchor: يعني إنك لا علم لك بكنهها ومدى عظمها

RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r13.claim: The interrogative mā is nominative, while adrāka is syntactically suspended by containing a question.
RAZI-FULL:v30p90/r13.anchor: و { أدراك } معلق عنه لتضمنه معنى الاستفهام

STUDYQURAN:69:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:intro/r1.claim: Al-Ḥāqqah is a late Makkan sūrah, generally dated shortly after al-Mulk, and named for the Day of Judgment in its opening verses.
STUDYQURAN:69:intro/r1.anchor: A late Makkan sūrah, al-Ḥāqqah is generally believed to have been revealed shortly after Sūrah 67, al-Mulk.

STUDYQURAN:69:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:intro/r2.claim: It links to the preceding sūrah by answering the charge that the Prophet was possessed and by describing Resurrection and Judgment more fully.
STUDYQURAN:69:intro/r2.anchor: the later verses provide a more complete response to the charge that the Prophet was possessed

STUDYQURAN:69:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:intro/r3.claim: The sūrah warns through earlier deniers, describes Judgment and the differing reception of the deeds' book, then reaffirms the Quran's revealed nature.
STUDYQURAN:69:intro/r3.anchor: The next section (vv. 13–17) describes some aspects of the Day of Judgment

STUDYQURAN:69:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:1/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:1/r1.claim: Ḥāqqah is an emphatic form of ḥaqq, meaning truth or reality; here it evokes the overwhelming, inevitable reality none can avoid.
STUDYQURAN:69:1/r1.anchor: Undeniable Reality translates ḥāqqah, which is an emphatic form ofḥaqq, meaning “truth” or “reality.”

STUDYQURAN:69:1/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:1/r2.speaker: All commentators
STUDYQURAN:69:1/r2.claim: All commentators agree that the Undeniable Reality refers to Resurrection and Judgment, though they differ over the aspect meant.
STUDYQURAN:69:1/r2.anchor: All commentators agree that the Undeniable Reality is a reference to the Day of Resurrection and Judgment

STUDYQURAN:69:1/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:1/r3.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:69:1/r3.claim: One view is that everything disbelievers rejected in earthly life will be realized and made evident.
STUDYQURAN:69:1/r3.anchor: all that was rejected by disbelievers in this life will be realized and made evident (JJ)

STUDYQURAN:69:1/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:1/r4.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:69:1/r4.claim: Another view is that everyone will see the true nature of their deeds, as in 67:11.
STUDYQURAN:69:1/r4.anchor: everyone will see the true nature of their deeds, as in 67:11

ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r1.claim: In the opening construction, the first al-ḥāqqa is a subject, mā is another subject, and the second al-ḥāqqa predicates mā and refers back to it.
ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r1.anchor: الأولة: مرفوع بالابتداء، و " ما " رفع بالابتداء أيضا.

ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r3.claim: Al-ḥāqqa means the Hour or Resurrection; it is so named because every good or evil deed a person does becomes real and established.
ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r3.anchor: والحاقة: الساعة والقيامة وسميت (الحاقة) لأنها تحق كل

TABATABAI:69:1-5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:1-5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:1-5/r1.claim: The sura names the Resurrection al-Haqqa and also al-Qari'a and al-Waqi'a; it first recalls destroyed deniers, then describes the Resurrection and people's fates, and finally affirms the Qur'an's truth. Its Meccan setting follows from its style.
TABATABAI:69:1-5/r1.anchor: تذكر الحاقة وهي القيامة وقد سمتها أيضا بالقارعة والواقعة. وقد ساقت الكلام فيها في فصول ثلاثة فصل تذكر فيه إجمالا

TABATABAI:69:1-5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:1-5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:1-5/r2.claim: Al-Haqqa means the Great Resurrection, named for its irrevocable, certain reality; haqq means an established and real fact.
TABATABAI:69:1-5/r2.anchor: المراد بالحاقة القيامة الكبرى سميت بها لثبوتها ثبوتا لا مرد له ولا ريب فيه، من حق الشيء بمعنى ثبت وتقرر

TABATABAI:69:1-5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:1-5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:1-5/r3.claim: The interrogative ما magnifies the event; repeating its name instead of a pronoun intensifies the emphasis, and the first question is predicated of al-Haqqa.
TABATABAI:69:1-5/r3.anchor: استفهامية تفيد تفخيم أمرها، ولذلك بعينه وضع الظاهر موضع الضمير ولم يقل ما هي، والجملة الاستفهامية خبر الحاقة.

THALABI:v10p25#3/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p25#3/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p25#3/r1.claim: Al-Ḥāqqah is the Resurrection: it is certain and has no false claimant, brings realities to light, and makes recompense due.
THALABI:v10p25#3/r1.anchor: الحاقة ما الحاقة وما أدراك ما الحاقة

THALABI:v10p25#3/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p25#3/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p25#3/r2.claim: The word ḥaqq means that something is due or obligatory; the Quran uses the idiom for punishment becoming due on unbelievers.
THALABI:v10p25#3/r2.anchor: إذا وجب بحق حقوقا، قال الله سبحانه: ولكن حقت كلمة العذاب

THALABI:v10p25#3/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p25#3/r3.speaker: الكسائي والمؤرخ
THALABI:v10p25#3/r3.claim: Al-Kisaʾi and al-Muʾarrij gloss al-Ḥāqqah as the Day of Truth and cite an Arabic idiom about recognizing someone's truth.
THALABI:v10p25#3/r3.anchor: وقال الكسائي والمؤرخ: الحاقة: يوم الحق، يقول العرب: لما عرفت الحق مني.

THALABI:v10p25#3/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p25#3/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p25#3/r4.claim: Al-Ḥāqqah and al-Ḥaqqah are variant forms with the same meaning.
THALABI:v10p25#3/r4.anchor: والحاقة والحقة هي ثلاث لغات بمعنى واحد

THALABI:v10p25#3/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p25#3/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p25#3/r5.claim: The first al-Ḥāqqah may be a subject whose predicate follows; alternatively it is explained by the second as an expression of wonder, like asking What is Zayd?
THALABI:v10p25#3/r5.anchor: والحاقة الأولى رفع بالابتداء وخبره فيما بعده، وقيل: الحاقة الأولى مرفوعة بالثانية

THALABI:v10p29/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p29/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p29/r1.claim: The cited verses about the sun turning red at each night's end and appearing alternately tormented or scourged were affirmed by the Prophet as true.
THALABI:v10p29/r1.anchor: والشمس تصبح كل آخر ليلة … حمراء تصبح لونها يتورد

THALABI:v10p29/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p29/r2.speaker: علي بن الحسن
THALABI:v10p29/r2.claim: Ali ibn al-Husayn relates that after air, the Pen, and light, God created the Throne from differently colored lights, including white light that became daylight.
THALABI:v10p29/r2.anchor: إن الله سبحانه خلق العرش رابعا لم يخلق قبله إلا ثلاثة أشياء: الهواء، والقلم، والنور

THALABI:v10p29/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p29/r3.speaker: علي بن الحسن
THALABI:v10p29/r3.claim: Ali ibn al-Husayn says the Throne comprises seventy trillion layers, each praising God in a distinct voice powerful enough to destroy mountains and palaces and sink seas if heard.
THALABI:v10p29/r3.anchor: ثم جعله سبعين ألف ألف ألف طبق ليس من ذلك طبق إلا يسبح بحمده

ASAD-NOTES:69:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:69:intro/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:69:intro/r1.claim: Asad dates the surah shortly after surah 67, around three or four years before the emigration to Medina.
ASAD-NOTES:69:intro/r1.anchor: REVEALED shortly after surah 67 (Al-Mulk), i.e., about three or four years before the Prophet's exodus to Medina.

ASAD-NOTES:69:1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:69:1/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:69:1/r1.claim: Asad renders al-haqqah as the laying-bare of truth, emphasizes its awe, and says its reality exceeds human conception.
ASAD-NOTES:69:1/r1.anchor: OH, THE LAYING-BARE of the truth! [1] (69:2) How awesome that laying-bare of the truth! (69:3) And what could make thee conceive

ASAD-NOTES:69:1#n1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:69:1#n1/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:69:1#n1/r1.claim: The Day of Resurrection and Judgment will disclose the true quality of each person's past life and deeds, revealing the destiny those deeds entail.
ASAD-NOTES:69:1#n1/r1.anchor: the Day of Resurrection and Judgment, on which man will become fully aware of the quality of his past life

ELMALILI:69:1/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:1/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:1/r1.claim: Al-Haqqa is undisputedly one of the names of the Resurrection, like al-Waqia and al-Saa, but commentators offer more than ten explanations of its relation to truth and realization.
ELMALILI:69:1/r1.anchor: “el- Hâkka”; “el-Vâkı‘a”, “es-Sâ‘a” gibi kıyamet gününün isimlerinden olduğunda ihtilâf yoktur

ELMALILI:69:1/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:1/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:1/r2.claim: One interpretation derives it from truth as something fixed and obligatory: the Hour whose arrival is certain and inevitable.
ELMALILI:69:1/r2.anchor: “Hak” sâbit ve vâcib mânasına olarak “el-Hâkka” vukū‘u vâcib

ELMALILI:69:1/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:1/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:1/r3.claim: Another interpretation makes it the Hour when matters are recognized in their true reality and things are disclosed.
ELMALILI:69:1/r3.anchor: kendisinde umûr hakikatiyle tanınacak, yani eşyânın hakikatini keşf ü izhar edecek Sâ‘at

ELMALILI:69:1/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:1/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:1/r4.claim: A further interpretation calls it the event containing affairs whose truth and occurrence are certain, such as reward and punishment.
ELMALILI:69:1/r4.anchor: havâkk-ı umûru hâvî, yani kendisinde sıdk u tahakkuku vâcib sâbit umûr ve ahvâl vâki‘olan

ELMALILI:69:1/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:1/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:1/r5.claim: Another gloss relates haqqa to a person's special, particular right, using the expression 'this is my own right.'

ELMALILI:69:1/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:1/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:1/r6.claim: Another interpretation is an unfailing calamity that comes and carries out what it will, as in the description that its occurrence has no lie.
ELMALILI:69:1/r6.anchor: şaşmaksızın inen ve yapacağını yalansız yapan musibet demektir

ELMALILI:69:1/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:1/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:1/r7.claim: It can also mean the appointed time whose occurrence has become due upon a people, close to the sense of an inevitable Hour.
ELMALILI:69:1/r7.anchor: Kavim üzerine vukū‘u hak olan vakit demektir

ELMALILI:69:1/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:1/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:1/r8.claim: It may refer to the time when every doer receives the true recompense for good or evil and every deed is requited.
ELMALILI:69:1/r8.anchor: her âmile amelinin hak olduğu vakit demektir ki o kıyamettir

ELMALILI:69:1/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:1/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:1/r9.claim: It is the Hour when all effects of people's deeds become fully realized and rewards and punishments come to pass.
ELMALILI:69:1/r9.anchor: Mükellefînin amellerinin hepsinin âsârı tamamıyla tahakkuk edip intizar haddinden çıktığı hak Sâ‘at

ELMALILI:69:1/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:1/r10.speaker: Ezherî
ELMALILI:69:1/r10.claim: Al-Haqqa can derive from overcoming in a contest: God overcomes those who challenge His religion with falsehood.
ELMALILI:69:1/r10.anchor: Ezherî’nin kavlince muhasama ve mügālebe mânasına حَاققته فحققته

ELMALILI:69:1/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:1/r11.speaker: Ebû Müslim
ELMALILI:69:1/r11.claim: Abu Muslim derives the active form from the phrase that the word of the Lord has come true.
ELMALILI:69:1/r11.anchor: Ebû Müslim’in kavlince “el-Hâkka”, حَقَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ

ELMALILI:69:1/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:1/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:1/r12.claim: Another analysis treats it as an abstract verbal noun like aqiba or afiya, meaning pure reality itself.
ELMALILI:69:1/r12.anchor: “Âkıbet”, “âfiyet” gibi masdardır ki mahz-ı hakikat demek olur

ELMALILI:69:1/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:1/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:1/r13.claim: A final view treats al-Haqqa simply as a proper name of Resurrection without any further intended meaning.
ELMALILI:69:1/r13.anchor: Kıyametin ismi olması itibariyle başkaca mefhum melhuz olmayarak ism-i câmiddir

ELMALILI:69:1/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:1/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:1/r14.claim: The many proposed nuances notwithstanding, the following question indicates that the Haqqa is not something one can know through unaided reasoning.
ELMALILI:69:1/r14.anchor: “el-Hâkka” وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ مَا ٱلْحَآقَّةُ buyurulduğu üzere dirayetle bilinir bir şey değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:1/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:1/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:1/r2.claim: The Resurrection is called al-Haqqa because it certainly occurs and reveals the real value and consequences of people's earthly deeds.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:1/r2.anchor: insanlar dünyada yapıp ettiklerinin gerçek değerini kavrayacakları ve sonuçlarını görecekleri için ona da “Hâkka” ismi verilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:1/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:1/r4.speaker: müfessirlerin büyük çoğunluğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:1/r4.claim: The great majority of commentators understand al-Haqqa to mean the Resurrection.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:1/r4.anchor: Müfessirlerin büyük çoğunluğu hâkka kelimesine “kıyamet” anlamı vermiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:1/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:1/r5.speaker: Ateş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:1/r5.claim: Some instead connect al-Haqqa with the crushing defeat that would befall Quraysh for opposing the Prophet, prompted by the following mention of punished peoples.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:1/r5.anchor: dünyada azaba uğramış kavimlerin anılmasından hareketle hâkka kelimesinden, Hz. Peygamber’e isyan eden Kureyş’in başına gelecek olan ağır yenilgiye dikkat çekildiği görüşünde olanlar da vardır (Ateş

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r1.claim: Al-Ḥāqqah resembles the preceding al-Wāqiʿah in affirming the Resurrection and depicting its terrors.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r1.anchor: both substantiate the Day of Judgement and portray the horrors of that Day.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r4.claim: Al-Ḥāqqah shares al-Qalam’s central theme, substantiating the Day of Judgement, though their arguments differ.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r4.anchor: Its central theme is the same as that of the previous sūrah: substantiation of the Day of Judgement.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r6.claim: Verses 1–12 cite earlier nations as evidence that rejecting messengers brings certain punishment in this world and the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r6.anchor: The history of various nations is cited as evidence

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p447/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p447/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p447/r1.claim: Al-Ḥāqqah names an event certain to occur according to common sense and morality; it is inevitable.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p447/r1.anchor: bound to happen as per the dictates of common sense and morality; something which is inevitable and certain to materialize.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p447/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p447/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p447/r2.claim: The word al-Ḥāqqah substitutes for an entire sentence.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p447/r2.anchor: This one word is actually a substitute for the whole sentence.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p447/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p447/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p447/r4.claim: The truncated, ambiguous wording jolts an indifferent addressee by focusing attention on the opening subject and drawing attention through uncertainty.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p447/r4.anchor: The khabar is not mentioned so that all the attention of the addressee is focused on the mubtadā’.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p447/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p447/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p447/r5.claim: As a name for the Day of Judgement, al-Ḥāqqah conveys both its certainty and why it must occur.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p447/r5.anchor: This name not only expresses the certainty of its happening but why it should necessarily happen

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p448/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p448/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p448/r1.claim: The rational and moral arguments for the Day’s necessity are explained in earlier sūrahs, with indications also in this and later sūrahs.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p448/r1.anchor: The arguments of both these aspects can also be seen in the exegesis of the previous sūrahs.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p448/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p448/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p448/r2.claim: Al-Ḥāqqah secondarily includes the inevitable punishment nations face for rejecting their messenger.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p448/r2.anchor: also included in it in a secondary manner is the punishment which a nation necessarily faces if it rejects its messenger.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p448/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p448/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p448/r3.claim: Punishment for rejecting a messenger prefigures and substantiates the Hereafter’s punishment because it follows rejection of that Day.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p448/r3.anchor: this punishment is a prelude to the punishment on the Day of Judgement and also its substantiation

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p448/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p448/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p448/r4.claim: Messengers warn of both the Hereafter and the punishment that follows denial; after the truth is conclusively conveyed, deniers’ punishment arrives, and every divine promise and messenger’s warning is true.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p448/r4.anchor: every warning of the messenger is true, hence, this punishment also is

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p312/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p312/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p312/r1.claim: Qatada explains the Event as the time when each people’s deeds come due for them.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p312/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ الحاقة ﴾ قال حقت لكل قوم أعمالهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p253/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p253/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p253/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan and follows the previous surah's mention of the fortunate, the wretched, and deniers by describing Resurrection and its rewards and punishments, with past destroyed peoples as warnings to Meccans.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p253/r1.anchor: هذه السورة مكية. ومناسبتها لما قبلها: أنه لما ذكر شيئا من أحوال السعداء والأشقياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p253/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p253/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p253/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others identify al-ḥāqqah as Resurrection and resurrection, when every worker meets the consequence of his deeds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p253/r2.anchor: الحاقة: المراد بها القيامة والبعث، قاله ابن عباس وغيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p253/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p253/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p253/r3.claim: Other explanations say it reveals realities, names the time when matters become real, or is an active participle from ḥaqqa, meaning something firmly established and beyond doubt.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p253/r3.anchor: لأنها تبدي حقائق الأشياء. وقيل: سميت بذلك لأن الأمر يحق فيها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p253/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p253/r4.speaker: الأزهري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p253/r4.claim: Al-Azharī explains the root through competition: the Resurrection is al-ḥāqqah because it defeats every opponent of God's religion who argues falsely.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p253/r4.anchor: وقال الأزهري: حاققته فحققته أحقه: أي غالبته فغلبته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p253/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p253/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p253/r5.claim: A further analysis treats al-ḥāqqah as a verbal noun like al-ʿāqibah.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p39#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p39#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p39#3/r1.claim: The name al-Haqqa may mean the Hour, an event whose occurrence must become real, a time in which true matters of reckoning and recompense are established, or a time when realities become known; Ibn Abbas transmits the last explanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p39#3/r1.anchor: أي الساعة أو الحالة التي يحق ويجب وقوعها أو التي تحقق وتثبت فيها الأمور الحقة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p39#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p39#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p39#3/r2.claim: On the last two senses the action is figuratively attributed to the Hour, properly belonging to the events or knowledgeable people within it; al-Kashf says this applies only to the final sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p39#3/r2.anchor: وإسناد الفعل لها على الوجهين الأخيرين مجاز وهو حقيقة لما فيها من الأمور أو لمن فيها من أولي العلم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p39#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p39#3/r3.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v29p39#3/r3.claim: Al-Kashf says the second sense may also be understood as a “possessor of realities” named after what accompanies it, and prefers this since the Hour and its contents are equally certain.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p39#3/r3.anchor: وفي الكشف كون الإسناد مجازيا إنما هو على الوجه الأخير

ALUSI-FULL:v29p39#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p39#3/r4.speaker: الأزهري
ALUSI-FULL:v29p39#3/r4.claim: Al-Azhari derives the name from overcoming an opponent in dispute: the Resurrection overcomes everyone who disputes God's religion falsely.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p39#3/r4.anchor: وقال الأزهري الحاقة القيامة من حاقته فحققته أي غالبته فغلبته

ALUSI-FULL:v29p39#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p39#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p39#3/r5.claim: It may be an adjective with its described noun omitted because the quality is unmistakable, a proper name for Judgment Day, or a verbal noun like “outcome”; in every case it begins the sentence whose predicate follows.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p39#3/r5.anchor: وظاهر كلامهم أنها على جميع ذلك وصف حذف موصوفه للإيذان بكمال ظهور اتصافه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p204#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p204#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p204#2/r1.claim: Al-Haqqa means the Resurrection, which has truly come to pass and cannot be denied; it also means the realities and recompense that become manifest and due.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p204#2/r1.anchor: {الحاقة} يعني القيامة سميت حاقة لأنها حقت فلا كاذبة لها. وقيل لأن فيها حواق الأمور وحقائقها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p204#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p204#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p204#2/r2.claim: The root haqq can mean that something becomes obligatory, as in the statement that the word of punishment became due against unbelievers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p204#2/r2.anchor: ولأن فيها يحق الجزاء على الأعمال، أي يجب يقال: حق عليه الشيء إذا وجب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p204#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p204#2/r3.speaker: الكسائي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p204#2/r3.claim: Al-Kisai glosses al-Haqqa as the Day of Truth.

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:2-4/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:2-4/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:2-4/r1.claim: Al-Ḥāqqah can mean the Hour, an event certain to occur, one in which realities become known, or one in which reckoning and recompense occur by figurative attribution.
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:2-4/r1.anchor: أي الساعة أو الحالة التي يحق وقوعها، أو التي تحق فيها الأمور

BIQAI-FULL:v8p119#s069/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p119#s069/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p119#s069/r1.claim: The surah establishes resurrection as the disclosure of truth and defeat of falsehood, displaying comprehensive knowledge, complete power, and justice that separates the faithful from sinners; its title states this plainly.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p119#s069/r1.anchor: تنزيه الخالق ببعث الخلائق لإحقاق الحق وإزهاق الباطل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p119#s069/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p119#s069/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p119#s069/r2.claim: The basmala praises God’s perfection and justice, universal generosity, and special favor for those who keep His limits.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p119#s069/r2.anchor: الذي عم جوده بالعدل كبرا ومجدا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p119#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p119#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p119#2/r1.claim: Al-Ḥāqqah is the certain Hour, where all matters appear in their realities and are judged justly; the name can mean both what is made true and what makes truth prevail over every opponent.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p119#2/r1.anchor: فهي ثابتة في نفسها , ومن إحضار الأمور فيها بحقائقها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p119#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p119#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p119#2/r4.claim: The preceding Sūrat Nūn warned against equating wrongdoers with the righteous and described judgment; the Day of Gathering is the Qur’an’s decisive reminder, and Jonah’s story demonstrates God’s power to bring it about.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p119#2/r4.anchor: وقصة صاحب الحوت عليه السلام أدل دليل على القدرة عليها

DURR-FULL:v8p263/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r1.claim: The chapter is Meccan and has fifty-two verses.
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r1.anchor: مكية وآياتها اثنتان وخمسون مقدمة السورة

DURR-FULL:v8p263/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Surat al-Haqqa was revealed in Mecca.
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: نزلت سورة الحاقة بمكة

DURR-FULL:v8p263/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r3.speaker: ابن الزبير
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r3.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr likewise says Surat al-Haqqa was revealed in Mecca.
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه عن ابن الزبير مثله

DURR-FULL:v8p263/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r4.speaker: أبو برزة
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r4.claim: Abu Barza says the Prophet used to recite al-Haqqa and similar chapters at dawn prayer.
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r4.anchor: عن أبي برزة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقرأ في الفجر بالحاقة ونحوها

DURR-FULL:v8p263/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r6.claim: Al-Haqqa is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: { الحاقة } قال: من أسماء يوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v8p263/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r7.claim: Al-Haqqa is the Hour, making each worker realize his deeds; the question magnifies the Resurrection, and al-Qariʿa also means the Hour.
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r7.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {الحاقة} يعني الساعة أحقت لكل عامل عمله {وما أدراك ما الحاقة} قال: تعظيما ليوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v8p263/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r8.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r8.claim: Al-Haqqa makes each worker's deed come true—faith for the believer, hypocrisy for the hypocrite—while al-Qariʿa means Resurrection Day.
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r8.anchor: عن ابن جريج رضي الله عنه في قوله: {الحاقة} قال: حققت لكل عامل عمله للمؤمن إيمانه وللمنافق نفاقه

RAZI-FULL:v32p68/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p68/r3.speaker: المحققون
RAZI-FULL:v32p68/r3.claim: The scholars say the Qariʿa formula is rhetorically stronger than the corresponding formula for the Real Event because later warning should intensify, but the Real Event is stronger semantically as justice, while the Calamity assaults hearts with terror.
RAZI-FULL:v32p68/r3.anchor: قال المحققون قوله : { القارعة * ما القارعة } أشد من قوله
